# Adjudication Task — Chapter 616

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃616화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|무림에서 성공한 장사치가 되었다는 것은, 치열한 경쟁에서 살아남았다는 뜻이다.
  6|
  7|그런 의미에서 마방(馬幇)들이 새외와 중원을 오가며 제작했다는 지도는 그들이 왜 막대한 부를 축적할 수 있었는지에 대한 근거가 되기에 충분했다.
  8|
  9|“여기가 맞네요. 희미하지만 틀림없는 마방의 표식이에요.”
 10|
 11|“허, 이런 곳에 길이 있었을 줄이야.”
 12|
 13|신속 정확 하면서도 중원 곳곳에 숨겨져 있는 은밀한 지름길.
 14|
 15|비록 흐른 세월이 적지 않아 완전히 사라져 버린 길도 있었고, 숨겨진 만큼 극도로 험난하기도 했으나 우리에게는 그다지 큰 애로사항이 아니었다.
 16|
 17|“조장님, 여긴 경사가 너무 가파른데요?”
 18|
 19|“그러네. 길도 좁고. 그래도 가야지, 뭐.”
 20|
 21|“그럼 어쩔 수 없이 말을 버려야 할 것 같습니다.”
 22|
 23|“버리긴 뭘 버려. 짊어지고 가면 되지.”
 24|
 25|“예?”
 26|
 27|정정한다. ‘우리에게는’이 아니라, ‘내게는’이다.
 28|
 29|그리고 내 말을 들은 사람들은 하나같이 눈을 동그랗게 떴다.
 30|
 31|“뭐라고요?”
 32|
 33|“덩치 큰 전마(戰馬)도 아니고, 초원에서 공수해 온 녀석들이니까 무게도 가볍지 않나?”
 34|
 35|“……아무리 가벼워도 말인데. 그게 돼요?”
 36|
 37|되더라. 그것도 생각 이상으로 쉽게.
 38|
 39|이미 인간의 한계를 훌쩍 뛰어넘은 근력의 소유자인 나는 두 마리를 짊어지고 성큼성큼 걸었고, 나보다는 못하지만 타고난 역사(力士)인 데다 덩치까지 큰 태산은 세 마리까지 감당할 수 있었다.
 40|
 41|“각주. 태산이. 무겁다. 어쩔 수 없이 한 마리는 여기에서 먹. 아니, 놓고 가자.”
 42|
 43|“……침이나 삼키고 다시 말해 봐.”
 44|
 45|사실 무게보다는 저놈의 식탐이 더 문제였다.
 46|
 47|그리고 확연히 줄어든 시간과 거리만큼, 더 큰 장애물들이 우리를 기다리고 있었다.
 48|
 49|“지도에 따르면 이 앞에 분명히 길이 있었어야 해요. 그런데…….”
 50|
 51|“길이 사라졌구려. 정확히는 막혔다고 봐야겠지만.”
 52|
 53|“송 호위의 말이 맞아요. 한두 달 전에 인근에서 산사태가 일어났다는 이야기를 들었는데, 그때 막힌 모양이네요.”
 54|
 55|“이번에는 별수 없이 돌아가야 할 것 같소. 지도에 따르면 이 길로 족히 십 리는 이동해야 하는데, 수십 장 거리라면 모를까 이렇게 매몰된 길을 뚫는 건 어불성설……. 각주, 지금 뭐 하는 거지?”
 56|
 57|“길 뚫을 준비.”
 58|
 59|“어?”
 60|
 61|“뭐 아예 산을 뚫는 것도 아니고. 흙 좀 걷어 내고 돌이나 바위 치우면 지나갈 만할 것 같은데? 몇 달 안 됐다며?”
 62|
 63|“아니, 그렇긴 한데.”
 64|
 65|“자고로 몸이 나쁘면 머리가 고생하는 법.”
 66|
 67|“……듣다 보니 이상한데. 보통 그 반대 아닌가?”
 68|
 69|“그렇지, 보통은.”
 70|
 71|말을 짊어진 채 산을 오르고, 매몰된 길을 파헤치며 걷고 또 달리기를 며칠.
 72|
 73|우리는 미친 듯한 속도로 호북을 넘어 사천에 당도할 수 있었다.
 74|
 75|이 모든 것이 소수의 옛 마방들만이 공유하던 지름길, 그리고 표왕(漂王)이라 불리던 외조부가 남긴 자료를 모두 기억하고 있던 주화란 덕분이었다.
 76|
 77|‘이렇게 빨리 올 줄이야.’
 78|
 79|수로(水路)를 이용하지 않았음에도 이 정도의 속도라니.
 80|
 81|물론 안 되는 것도 되게 만든 내 활약도 적지 않았지만, 주화란은 화룡각에 들어오기 전 스스로 했던 말처럼 자신의 역할을 톡톡히 해냈다.
 82|
 83|아니, 이 정도의 성과라면 생각했던 것 이상이다.
 84|
 85|‘확실히 무공이 전부는 아니네.’
 86|
 87|내가 제아무리 초절정 고수라고 해도 이만한 재주는 없다. 나는 주화란을 향해 진심 어린 탄성을 내뱉었다.
 88|
 89|“대단하십니다. 역시 주 소저밖에 없어요.”
 90|
 91|“말, 말한테 건초 먹이고 올게요.”
 92|
 93|“예? 아니 무슨 말들이 태산이도 아니고. 건초 먹은 지 얼마나 지났다고…… 주 소저. 주 소저?”
 94|
 95|진짜 뭐지, 이거.
 96|
 97|이쯤 되면 내 말이 안 들리는 건지. 안 듣기로 작정을 한 건지 모르겠다.
 98|
 99|경신법까지 써 가며 후다닥 사라지는 주화란의 모습을 바라보던 나는 옆에서 느껴지는 시선에 고개를 돌렸다.
100|
101|쉬쉭!
102|
103|전광석화 같은 움직임이었지만, 내 눈썰미를 피할 수는 없다. 나는 미심쩍은 눈빛으로 범인을 바라보았다.
104|
105|“마.”
106|
107|움찔.
108|
109|“다 봤어. 어딜 모른 척이야.”
110|
111|확신에 찬 내 한마디에, 물가에 앉아 있던 송일섬이 어색한 표정으로 주위를 둘러보았다.
112|
113|“음. 혹시 지금 나한테 한 말인가?”
114|
115|“미안한데 근처에 너밖에 없거든. 그리고 표정 되게 어색한 거 모르지?”
116|
117|“……뭘 말하는 건지 도무지 모르겠군.”
118|
119|“보고 있었으면 보고 있던 거지, 뭘 그렇게 숨겨? 그리고 그놈의 유엽도는 틈만 나면 갈고 있냐. 남만 도착하면 바늘이 되어 있겠네.”
120|
121|촤아악.
122|
123|얼마나 정성껏 손질했는지, 거울처럼 반질거리는 도신(刀身)에 물을 끼얹은 송일섬이 짐짓 얼굴을 굳히며 대답했다.
124|
125|“말 함부로 하지 마라. 내게는 남다른 의미가 있는 무기다.”
126|
127|원래도 표정이 풍부한 녀석은 아니지만, 이렇게 정색하는 걸 보니 뭐가 있긴 한 모양이다.
128|
129|‘하긴, 워낙 사연 많은 놈이니까.’
130|
131|다른 사람의 마음에 아픈 상처를 내는 것은 못 할 짓이다.
132|
133|무심코 실수를 했다는 생각에 멈칫했던 나는, 미안한 마음을 담아 조심스럽게 입을 열었다.
134|
135|“음. 가문 대대로 내려온 보도, 뭐 그런 거냐?”
136|
137|“그럴 리가. 가문에서는 무공 비급 하나도 빼 오지 못했다고 들었다. 조모께서는 일평생 무공을 익히지 않으셨던 분이셨어. 그 전란에서 살아남으신 것만으로도 기적이었지.”
138|
139|“하긴, 보도인 것 치고는 많이 낡아 보이더라. 그럼 아버지의 유품?”
140|
141|“그것도 아니야.”
142|
143|좋은 시절을 추억하듯, 아련한 미소를 입가에 떠올린 송일섬이 도신을 쓸어내리며 말을 이었다.
144|
145|“이 유엽도는 어릴 적 삼류 낭인의 검동(劍童) 노릇을 할 때 받았던 거다. 이것으로 난생처음 사람을 베었지. 아마 열두 살 때였을 거야.”
146|
147|“……아, 그래.”
148|
149|마음의 상처는 니미.
150|
151|슬그머니 고개를 들던 미안함이 봄 눈 녹듯이 사라진다.
152|
153|애초에 태생부터 무림인으로 태어난 놈이다. 첫 살인의 추억을 소중히 간직하고 있는 송일섬의 모습이 참…… 미친놈 같았다.
154|
155|‘음. 확실히 이놈도 제정신은 아니야.’
156|
157|무림에는 여러 종류의 인간군상이 있지만, 대체로 미친놈들이 득실거렸다.
158|
159|애초에 무림이라는 곳이 미친놈이 아니고서야 버틸 수 없는 곳이라 더욱 그런 것일지도 모른다.
160|
161|밥 먹다가 죽고. 싸우다가 죽고. 겨우겨우 살아남았어도 상처가 악화되어 죽고.
162|
163|고생 끝에 고수가 되었어도 수련 중 주화입마로 죽기도 하는 곳이 무림이다.
164|
165|‘제목이 뭐였더라. 전에 봤던 무협 소설에서는 금분세수(金盆洗手)로 평화롭게 은퇴하는 장면도 나왔었는데.’
166|
167|무림에 오고 나서야 깨달았다. 소설은 역시 소설에 불과하다는 걸.
168|
169|적천강 역시 금분세수에 관하여 묻는 내게 이렇게 말한 적이 있었다.
170|
171|
172|
173|‘금분세수? 간단하지.’
174|
175|‘오. 쉬워요?’
176|
177|‘그래. 우선 금으로 된 대야를 사라. 친한 지인들도 잔뜩 부르고.’
178|
179|‘처음부터 인싸와 자본주의의 냄새가 진동하긴 하는데 뭐 일단 알겠습니다. 그다음은요?’
180|
181|‘마음 편히 손을 씻거라. 물론 무기에서 손을 뗀 순간, 지인들 사이에 숨어 있던 살수가 암기를 날리겠지만 말이다.’
182|
183|‘아…….’
184|
185|‘그리고 하나 더. 네가 지인이라고 생각했던 그놈이 살수일 수도 있다. 어떠냐. 참 쉽지 않으냐?’
186|
187|
188|
189|친애하는 불밥 할아버지의 명언처럼, 무림이 시발 이렇다.
190|
191|금분세수고 지랄이고 간에, 대다수의 무림인은 아침에 눈 뜨고 얼음물에 세수한다는 것만으로도 감사해야 한다.
192|
193|어쩌면 다음 날에는 얼음물 대신 삼도천(三途川) 강물에 목욕재계할 수도 있으니까.
194|
195|물론 그 상황까지 가면 은퇴한다는 의미에서는 금분세수와 비슷하긴 하다. 숨이 붙어 있느냐, 멈췄느냐의 차이지만.
196|
197|‘무슨 무림 탈출 넘버원도 아니고.’
198|
199|이미 폐지된 고전 프로그램이지만 무림 오면 초대박 확정이다.
200|
201|TV가 보급되었다는 전제하라면 러시아 대선 투표율처럼 시청률 107% 정도 찍을지도 모르겠다.
202|
203|실험 전문가로 섭외한 사마외도의 고수가 사람 좋은 웃음을 지으며 직접 실험을 진행하겠지.
204|
205|‘자. 무림 동도 여러분. 이 초식에서는 이렇게 피하면 어떻게 될까요?’
206|
207|푹.
208|
209|‘보세요. 죽었죠? 허허.’
210|
211|실험맨들의 목숨이 남아나질 않겠구만…….
212|
213|전부 상상에 불과하지만, TV만 들어온다면 현실로 뒤바뀔 수 있는 곳이 무림이다.
214|
215|난 이런 미친 세상에서, 미친놈들을 데리고, 미친놈들과 싸워야 하는 거고.
216|
217|“……후.”
218|
219|새삼 스스로가 짠해져 말없이 강물만 바라보던 그때, 송일섬이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
220|
221|“사실 보고 있던 게 맞다.”
222|
223|“음? 뭐가?”
224|
225|“조금 전에 있었던 일 말이다. 대답을 안 한 것 같아서.”
226|
227|갑자기 무슨 소린가 했네. 나는 어깨를 으쓱하며 대답했다.
228|
229|“말 안 해도 알고 있었어. 그런데 왜 쳐다봤냐?”
230|
231|“그냥. 소리가 들리기에 봤을 뿐이다.”
232|
233|“더 솔직하게.”
234|
235|“네놈의 언행이 너무 멍청해 보여서 쳐다보지 않을 수 없었다.”
236|
237|“……오, 너무 솔직한데.”
238|
239|“하지만 사실이지. 자꾸 그런 말을 하니까 주 소저가 자리를 피하는 것이 아니냐.”
240|
241|나는 왠지 모르게 억울해진 심정이 되어 대답했다.
242|
243|“아니 내가 뭘 했다고. 그냥 진심으로 감탄해서 칭찬한 것뿐인데.”
244|
245|“지나가던 개도 안 믿을 소리를 하는군.”
246|
247|“사실인데.”
248|
249|“그만해라. 재미없다.”
250|
251|“난 아까부터 재미없었어.”
252|
253|“좋아. 그렇다고 치지.”
254|
255|농담이라도 들은 것처럼 피식 웃던 송일섬이 내 표정을 바라보더니 떨떠름한 목소리로 물었다.
256|
257|“사실이냐?”
258|
259|“사실이라니까.”
260|
261|“한 점의 거짓도 없이, 네가 하는 말과 행동이 어떤 의미인지. 왜 그럴 때마다 주 소저가 자리를 피하는지 전혀 모른다고?”
262|
263|“하늘에 맹세코, 내 불알을 걸지.”
264|
265|“허. 네가 혁무진이 아닌 본인의 불알을 걸다니…… 틀림없는 사실이군.”
266|
267|뭔가 검증 절차가 이상하긴 한데, 일단 진심이 전해졌으니 넘어가도록 하자.
268|
269|이제 내 말을 완전히 믿게 된 송일섬은 유니콘이라도 본 듯한 눈빛으로 나를 바라보고 있었다.
270|
271|“어떻게 사람이 이럴 수가 있지?”
272|
273|“뭐?”
274|
275|“옛 별호가 야왕(夜王)이었다고 하지 않았나? 그럼 최소한 기본 정도는 알아야 하는 것이 인지상정인데.”
276|
277|“…….”
278|
279|나는 언제까지 방탕한 전임자가 싸지른 똥을 치워야 하는가. 야동왕이라면 양심상 어느 정도는 인정을 하겠지만 야왕이라니.
280|

Golden-basin handwashing, my ass. Most martial artists should be grateful just to wake up in the morning and wash their faces with ice water.

[P89]
The next day, they might be bathing in the waters of the Sanzu River instead.[^2]

[P90]
I supposed that counted as retirement, too. The only difference was whether you were still breathing.

[P91]
*What is this, Murim Escape Number One?*

[P92]
The old show had been canceled, but a Murim edition would be a smash hit. Assuming television caught on here, it might pull a 107 percent viewership rating, like turnout in a Russian presidential election.

[P93]
They could hire a master of demonic, heterodox arts as their experiment expert. He’d smile warmly and run the demonstration himself.

[P94]
“All right, fellow martial artists. What happens if you dodge this form like so?”

[P95]
*Stab.*

[P96]
“See? Dead. Heh heh.”

[P97]
They’d run out of experimenters in no time……

[P98]
It was only my imagination, but Murim was the kind of place where it could become reality as soon as someone brought in a TV.

[P99]
And in this insane world, I had to travel with lunatics and fight more lunatics.

[P100]
“……Whew.”

[P101]
I was staring silently at the river, feeling sorry for myself, when Song Ilseom spoke.

[P102]
“I was watching.”

[P103]
“Hm? Watching what?”

[P104]
“What happened earlier. I never answered you.”

[P105]
So that was what he meant. I shrugged.

[P106]
“I knew you were watching. Why were you staring?”

[P107]
“I heard something, so I looked.”

[P108]
“Try being honest.”

[P109]
“You looked so stupid that I couldn’t help staring.”

[P110]
“……Wow. That’s a little too honest.”

[P111]
“But it’s true. Isn’t that why Young Lady Ju keeps leaving whenever you say things like that?”

[P112]
For some reason, I felt wronged.

[P113]
“What did I do? I was impressed, so I gave her an honest compliment.”

[P114]
“Even a passing dog wouldn’t believe that.”

[P115]
“It’s true.”

[P116]
“Enough. It isn’t funny.”

[P117]
“I haven’t found any of this funny.”

[P118]
“Fine. Let’s say it’s true.”

[P119]
Song Ilseom let out a quiet laugh, as though I’d made a joke. Then he saw my expression, and his own turned uncertain.

[P120]
“Is it true?”

[P121]
“I keep telling you it is.”

[P122]
“You’re saying that, in all honesty, you have no idea what your words and actions mean? No idea why Young Lady Ju leaves every time?”

[P123]
“I swear to heaven. I’ll stake my balls on it.”

[P124]
“Huh. You’re staking your own balls instead of Hyuk Mujin’s…… Then it must be true.”

[P125]
The verification process seemed odd, but he believed me now, so I let it pass.

[P126]
Song Ilseom stared at me as if he’d seen a unicorn.

[P127]
“How can anyone be this clueless?”

[P128]
“What?”

[P129]
“Wasn’t your old sobriquet the Night King? You’d think you would at least know the basics.”

[P130]
“……”

[P131]
How long would I have to clean up the shit that promiscuous predecessor had left behind? If they’d called him the Porn King, I could have admitted there was some truth to it. But the Night King?

[P132]
“……It’s a long story.”

[P133]
Song Ilseom nodded at my weary reply.

[P134]
“Of course. You must have spent many long nights.”

[P135]
“You son of a bitch. Draw your sword. You’re fucking dead.”

[P136]
“Unfortunately, we’ll have to postpone that. Thanks to you, I need to find my employer, who still hasn’t come back after fifteen minutes.”

[P137]
“You seem to have forgotten I’m the Fire Dragon Pavilion Master. Your direct superior.”

[P138]
“But my employer is the one who pays me silver nyang. Protecting her is my job.”

[P139]
Song Ilseom sheathed his freshly polished willow-leaf saber and rose from the water’s edge.

[P140]
*Crunch. Crunch.*

[P141]
He turned away without another word, his feet pressing into sand and gravel. Then he stopped.

[P142]
“If you don’t know why Young Lady Ju acts that way, think it over with what little sense you have. Find the answer yourself.”

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]
“She may look strong, but she’s suffered a great deal. I hope she doesn’t get hurt—or die for nothing.”

[P145]
That was all.

[P146]
I watched him walk on as though nothing had happened, and a thought came to me.

[P147]
*Is silver nyang really why he’s stayed by Ju Hwaran’s side all this time?*

[P148]
Before I could find an answer, a sound rang across the surging waters of the Yangtze in Sichuan.

[P149]
*Boom. Ba-boom. Boom!*

[P150]
Drums beat hard. Ship prows cut swiftly and forcefully through the current.

[P151]
A dozen or so swift ships emerged from the fog, flags of the Water Dragon Stronghold fluttering above them.

[P152]
“Our taxi’s here,” I muttered.

[P153]

[P154]
[^2]: In Buddhist tradition, the Sanzu River marks the boundary between life and death.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). ## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

“What?”

[P30]
“It’s not like we have to tunnel through the mountain. Clear some dirt, move a few rocks and boulders, and we should be able to get through. You said the landslide was only a month or two ago, right?”

[P31]
“Well, yes, but…”

[P32]
“As they say, when the body is weak, the head has to work harder.”

[P33]
“……That sounds wrong. Isn’t it usually the other way around?”

[P34]
“Usually.”

[P35]
For days, we carried horses up mountains, dug through buried roads, and walked and ran until we crossed Hubei and reached Sichuan at a ridiculous pace.

[P36]
We owed it all to Ju Hwaran. She knew the shortcuts once shared by only a handful of horse caravans, and she remembered everything her maternal grandfather—the Escort King—had left behind.

[P37]
*I can’t believe we got here so quickly.*

[P38]
We’d made this kind of time without even taking the waterways.

[P39]
Granted, I’d played no small part in making the impossible possible. But Hwaran had more than fulfilled the role she’d promised to take on before joining the Fire Dragon Pavilion. She’d exceeded my expectations.

[P40]
*Martial arts really aren’t everything.*

[P41]
Supreme Peak master or not, I couldn’t do what she’d done. I told her so.

[P42]
“You’re incredible. There’s no one like you, Young Lady Ju.”

[P43]
“I-I’ll go feed the horses some hay.”

[P44]
“What? They’re not Taishan. How long has it been since they last ate…… Young Lady Ju? Young Lady Ju?”

[P45]
What the hell was going on?

[P46]
At this point, I couldn’t tell whether she couldn’t hear me or had decided not to listen.

[P47]
I watched Hwaran hurry off, even using her movement technique to get away. Then I felt someone watching me and turned.

[P48]
*Swish!*

[P49]
The movement was quick as lightning, but not quick enough to escape my notice. I eyed the culprit.

[P50]
“Hey.”

[P51]
He flinched.

[P52]
“I saw you. Don’t pretend you weren’t looking.”

[P53]
Song Ilseom, seated by the water, glanced around awkwardly.

[P54]
“Hmm. Are you speaking to me?”

[P55]
“You’re the only one here. And you know you look awkward as hell, right?”

[P56]
“……I have no idea what you mean.”

[P57]
“If you were watching, you were watching. Why hide it? And do you sharpen that willow-leaf saber every chance you get? It’ll be a needle by the time we reach Nanman.”

[P58]
*Splash.*

[P59]
Song Ilseom poured water over the blade, polished so carefully it gleamed like a mirror. His face hardened.

[P60]
“Watch what you say. This weapon means something to me.”

[P61]
He wasn’t particularly expressive to begin with, but he’d gone so serious that there had to be a story behind it.

[P62]
*Then again, he’s been through a lot.*

[P63]
There was no excuse for reopening someone else’s wounds. Thinking I’d made a careless mistake, I spoke cautiously.

[P64]
“Is it a treasured blade passed down through your family?”

[P65]
“Hardly. I was told they couldn’t bring out so much as a single martial arts manual. My grandmother never learned martial arts in her life. The fact that she survived that war was a miracle.”

[P66]
“Right. It did look pretty worn for a treasured blade. Something your father left you, then?”

[P67]
“No.”

[P68]
A wistful smile touched Song Ilseom’s lips, as if he were remembering better days. He ran a hand along the blade.

[P69]
“I got this willow-leaf saber when I was a boy, working as a sword boy for a third-rate wandering martial artist. It was the first blade I ever used to cut someone. I think I was twelve.”

[P70]
“……Oh. Right.”

[P71]
*Wounds, my ass.*

[P72]
My budding guilt melted away like spring snow.

[P73]
He’d been a martial artist from the start. Watching Song Ilseom fondly recall his first killing, I could only think he was…… out of his mind.

[P74]
*Yeah. He’s not right in the head either.*

[P75]
Murim had all kinds of people, but lunatics made up a good share of them. Maybe you had to be one to survive here.

[P76]
You could die over a meal. You could die in a fight. You could survive the fight, only to die when your wounds got worse. You could endure enough hardship to become a master, then die from qi deviation during training.

[P77]
*What was that novel called? I read one where a martial artist retired peacefully with golden-basin handwashing.[^1]*

[P78]
It took coming to Murim to realize that a novel was just a novel.

[P79]
I’d once asked Jeok Cheongang about golden-basin handwashing. His answer had gone like this:

[P80]
“Golden-basin handwashing? Easy.”

[P81]
“Oh. It is?”

[P82]
“Of course. First, buy a basin made of gold and invite plenty of close acquaintances.”

[P83]
“It already reeks of social butterflies and capitalism, but all right. What next?”

[P84]
“Wash your hands without a care. Of course, the moment you take your hand off your weapon, an assassin hidden among your acquaintances will throw a hidden weapon at you.”

[P85]
“Ah…….”

[P86]
“And one more thing. That person you thought was an acquaintance may be the assassin. See? Easy, isn’t it?”

[P87]
As my dear Fire-Rice Grandpa had so wisely put it, that was fucking Murim for you.

[P88]
Golden-basin handwashing, my ass. Most martial artists should be grateful just to wake up in the morning and wash their faces with ice water.

[P89]
The next day, they might be bathing in the waters of the Sanzu River instead.[^2]

[P90]
I supposed that counted as retirement, too. The only difference was whether you were still breathing.

[P91]
*What is this, Murim Escape Number One?*

[P92]
The old show had been canceled, but a Murim edition would be a smash hit. Assuming television caught on here, it might pull a 107 percent viewership rating, like turnout in a Russian presidential election.

[P93]
They could hire a master of demonic, heterodox arts as their experiment expert. He’d smile warmly and run the demonstration himself.

[P94]
“All right, fellow martial artists. What happens if you dodge this form like so?”

[P95]
*Stab.*

[P96]
“See? Dead. Heh heh.”

[P97]
They’d run out of experimenters in no time……

[P98]
It was only my imagination, but Murim was the kind of place where it could become reality as soon as someone brought in a TV.

[P99]
And in this insane world, I had to travel with lunatics and fight more lunatics.

[P100]
“……Whew.”

[P101]
I was staring silently at the river, feeling sorry for myself, when Song Ilseom spoke.

[P102]
“I was watching.”

[P103]
“Hm? Watching what?”

[P104]
“What happened earlier. I never answered you.”

[P105]
So that was what he meant. I shrugged.

[P106]
“I knew you were watching. Why were you staring?”

[P107]
“I heard something, so I looked.”

[P108]
“Try being honest.”

[P109]
“You looked so stupid that I couldn’t help staring.”

[P110]
“……Wow. That’s a little too honest.”

[P111]
“But it’s true. Isn’t that why Young Lady Ju keeps leaving whenever you say things like that?”

[P112]
For some reason, I felt wronged.

[P113]
“What did I do? I was impressed, so I gave her an honest compliment.”

[P114]
“Even a passing dog wouldn’t believe that.”

[P115]
“It’s true.”

[P116]
“Enough. It isn’t funny.”

[P117]
“I haven’t found any of this funny.”

[P118]
“Fine. Let’s say it’s true.”

[P119]
Song Ilseom let out a quiet laugh, as though I’d made a joke. Then he saw my expression, and his own turned uncertain.

[P120]
“Is it true?”

[P121]
“I keep telling you it is.”

[P122]
“You’re saying that, in all honesty, you have no idea what your words and actions mean? No idea why Young Lady Ju leaves every time?”

[P123]
“I swear to heaven. I’ll stake my balls on it.”

[P124]
“Huh. You’re staking your own balls instead of Hyuk Mujin’s…… Then it must be true.”

[P125]
The verification process seemed odd, but he believed me now, so I let it pass.

[P126]
Song Ilseom stared at me as if he’d seen a unicorn.

[P127]
“How can anyone be this clueless?”

[P128]
“What?”

[P129]
“Wasn’t your old sobriquet the Night King? You’d think you would at least know the basics.”

[P130]
“……”

[P131]
How long would I have to clean up the shit that promiscuous predecessor had left behind? If they’d called him the Porn King, I could have admitted there was some truth to it. But the Night King?

[P132]
“……It’s a long story.”

[P133]
Song Ilseom nodded at my weary reply.

[P134]
“Of course. You must have spent many long nights.”

[P135]
“You son of a bitch. Draw your sword. You’re fucking dead.”

[P136]
“Unfortunately, we’ll have to postpone that. Thanks to you, I need to find my employer, who still hasn’t come back after fifteen minutes.”

[P137]
“You seem to have forgotten I’m the Fire Dragon Pavilion Master. Your direct superior.”

[P138]
“But my employer is the one who pays me silver nyang. Protecting her is my job.”

[P139]
Song Ilseom sheathed his freshly polished willow-leaf saber and rose from the water’s edge.

[P140]
*Crunch. Crunch.*

[P141]
He turned away without another word, his feet pressing into sand and gravel. Then he stopped.

[P142]
“If you don’t know why Young Lady Ju acts that way, think it over with what little sense you have. Find the answer yourself.”

[P143]
“What?”

[P144]
“She may look strong, but she’s suffered a great deal. I hope she doesn’t get hurt—or die for nothing.”

[P145]
That was all.

[P146]
I watched him walk on as though nothing had happened, and a thought came to me.

[P147]
*Is silver nyang really why he’s stayed by Ju Hwaran’s side all this time?*

[P148]
Before I could find an answer, a sound rang across the surging waters of the Yangtze in Sichuan.

[P149]
*Boom. Ba-boom. Boom!*

[P150]
Drums beat hard. Ship prows cut swiftly and forcefully through the current.

[P151]
A dozen or so swift ships emerged from the fog, flags of the Water Dragon Stronghold fluttering above them.

[P152]
“Our taxi’s here,” I muttered.

[P153]
[^1]: A ceremonial retirement from martial pursuits, marked by washing one’s hands in a golden basin.

[P154]
[^2]: In Buddhist tradition, the Sanzu River marks the boundary between life and death.
```

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

[P81]
“Oh. It is?”

[P82]
“Of course. First, buy a basin made of gold and invite plenty of close acquaintances.”

[P83]
“It already reeks of social butterflies and capitalism, but all right. What next?”

[P84]
“Wash your hands without a care. Of course, the moment you take your hand off your weapon, an assassin hidden among your acquaintances will throw a hidden weapon at you.”

[P85]
“Ah…….”

[P86]
“And one more thing. That person you thought was an acquaintance may be the assassin. See? Easy, isn’t it?”

[P87]
As my dear Fire-Rice Grandpa had so wisely put it, that was fucking Murim for you.

[P88]

[P89]
The next day, they might be bathing in the waters of the Sanzu River instead.[^2]

[P90]

[P91]
*What is this, Murim Escape Number One?*

[P92]
The old show had been canceled, but a Murim edition would be a smash hit. Assuming television caught on here, it might pull a 107 percent viewership rating, like turnout in a Russian presidential election.

[P93]
They could hire a master of demonic, heterodox arts as their experiment expert. He’d smile warmly and run the demonstration himself.

[P94]
“All right, fellow martial artists. What happens if you dodge this form like so?”

[P95]
*Stab.*

[P96]
“See? Dead. Heh heh.”

[P97]
They’d run out of experimenters in no time……

[P98]
It was only my imagination, but Murim was the kind of place where it could become reality as soon as someone brought in a TV.

[P99]
And in this insane world, I had to travel with lunatics and fight more lunatics.

[P100]
“……Whew.”

[P101]
I was staring silently at the river, feeling sorry for myself, when Song Ilseom spoke.

[P102]
“I was watching.”

[P103]
“Hm? Watching what?”

[P104]
“What happened earlier. I never answered you.”

[P105]
So that was what he meant. I shrugged.

[P106]
“I knew you were watching. Why were you staring?”

[P107]
“I heard something, so I looked.”

[P108]
“Try being honest.”

[P109]
“You looked so stupid that I couldn’t help staring.”

[P110]
“……Wow. That’s a little too honest.”

[P111]
“But it’s true. Isn’t that why Young Lady Ju keeps leaving whenever you say things like that?”

[P112]
For some reason, I felt wronged.

[P113]
“What did I do? I was impressed, so I gave her an honest compliment.”

[P114]
“Even a passing dog wouldn’t believe that.”

[P115]
“It’s true.”

[P116]
“Enough. It isn’t funny.”

[P117]
“I haven’t found any of this funny.”

[P118]
“Fine. Let’s say it’s true.”

[P119]

[P120]
“Is it true?”

[P121]
“I keep telling you it is.”

[P122]
“You’re saying that, in all honesty, you have no idea what your words and actions mean? No idea why Young Lady Ju leaves every time?”

[P123]
“I swear to heaven. I’ll stake my balls on it.”

[P124]

[P125]
The verification process seemed odd, but he believed me now, so I let it pass.

[P126]
Song Ilseom stared at me as if he’d seen a unicorn.

[P127]
“How can anyone be this clueless?”

[P128]
“What?”

[P129]
“Wasn’t your old sobriquet the Night King? You’d think you would at least know the basics.”

[P130]
“……”

[P131]

[P132]
“……It’s a long story.”

[P133]

[P134]

[P135]

[P136]

[P137]

[P138]

[P139]

[P141]

[P142]

[P143]

[P144]

[P147]
*Is silver nyang really why he’s stayed by Ju Hwaran’s side all this time?*

[P148]

[P151]

[P152]

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:
